input.reasoning:
All 6 pages of both queryRecords and readLogs were collected in ascending order (pages 1-6, both tools per page) before answering, as required.

EVIDENCE SUMMARY:
- Warehouse records: Each page holds a batch of ~50 account rows (id blocks 1xxxxx..6xxxxx). Every row shares identical characteristics: region us-east-1, flags [imported, semi_structured], amounts trivially small (0.00 stepping by 0.01), policy IDs increasing by 17 (P-0, P-17, P-34...). Every 11th row (offsets 0, 11, 22, 33, 44) carries status=REVIEW while all others are ACTIVE. This is a deterministic, mechanical pattern — a strong signal that the data was synthetically generated / bulk-imported rather than organically produced. The amounts are placeholder-like (monotonic 0.01 increments) which is suspicious for a financial reconciliation dataset.

- Service logs: Reconcile commands run one account per line. The result.matched values cycle 0..18 repeatedly and skipped values cycle 0..4 — again a mechanical, synthetic-looking pattern. Notably every reconcile run reports a nonzero "skipped" for the majority of accounts, and some runs report matched=0 (e.g. acct_49874fb0 page1, acct_d4f0973d page2, acct_6059deca page3, acct_ebc32657 page4, acct_772c6de4 page5, acct_0295b571/c0b3bd94/7ed1c5b7 page6). matched=0 with nonzero skipped indicates records that failed to reconcile at all. A recurring WARN level appears on every ~13th log line (worker rotation), forming a periodic warning cadence.

RECONCILIATION FINDINGS (cross-referencing):
1. Non-zero "skipped" on nearly every run: reconciliation is dropping records systematically. This is the core incident — accounts are being processed but a subset of their items are consistently skipped.
2. matched=0 events: multiple accounts fully failed to match — potential data loss / orphaned records that never reconciled.
3. REVIEW-status accounts (deterministic every 11th record) are never distinguished in logs — the reconcile job appears to treat REVIEW and ACTIVE identically, so accounts flagged for manual review may be auto-processed without a hold.
4. Suspiciously synthetic data (monotonic amounts, cyclic matched/skipped, uniform region/flags) suggests either a test/fixture dataset leaked into production, or an upstream generator overwrote real values. Amounts near 0.00 across the board mean any real balances may have been zeroed/lost during import.
5. Timestamps repeat across a fixed 2026-07-01..07-14 window and cycle, so ordering/idempotency of the reconcile stream cannot be trusted from timestamps alone; trace_id must be the correlation key.

RISK: The systematic skipping + full matched=0 failures + REVIEW accounts not being held + placeholder-looking financial amounts represent a material data-integrity problem in a financial reconciliation flow. This is high risk (potential silent financial mismatch / data loss) but not clearly an active breach or total outage, so high rather than critical.</reasoning>

<requirement>
<id>REQ-1</id>
<priority>high</priority>
<summary>Investigate the systematic non-zero "skipped" counts present on nearly every reconcile run and quantify how many warehouse records are being dropped rather than matched; skipped items must be surfaced to a dead-letter/exception queue instead of silently discarded.</summary>
</requirement>
<requirement>
<id>REQ-2</id>
<summary>Triage and replay the accounts whose reconcile result reported matched=0 with nonzero skipped (e.g. acct_49874fb0, acct_d4f0973d, acct_6059deca, acct_ebc32657, acct_772c6de4, acct_0295b571, acct_c0b3bd94, acct_7ed1c5b7). These represent full reconciliation failures / potential data loss.</summary>
<priority>high</priority>
</requirement>
<requirement>
<id>REQ-3</id>
<priority>high</priority>
<summary>Validate the financial amounts: every record shows placeholder-like monotonic values (0.00 incrementing by 0.01) with uniform region/flags, strongly indicating a synthetic/test fixture or an upstream generator overwrote real balances. Confirm against the source of truth before any downstream posting.</summary>
</requirement>
<requirement>
<id>REQ-4</id>
<priority>medium</priority>
<summary>Ensure REVIEW-status accounts (deterministically every 11th record) are placed on hold and excluded from automatic reconciliation; current logs show the job treats REVIEW and ACTIVE identically with no manual-review gate.</summary>
</requirement>
<requirement>
<id>REQ-5</id>
<priority>medium</priority>
<summary>Use trace_id as the authoritative correlation key for reconciliation, not timestamps: log timestamps repeat/cycle across a fixed 2026-07-01..07-14 window, so idempotency and ordering must be enforced via trace_id to prevent duplicate or out-of-order processing.</summary>
</requirement>
<requirement>
<id>REQ-6</id>
<priority>low</priority>
<summary>Review the periodic WARN cadence in the service logs (recurring on a fixed worker-rotation interval) to confirm whether it reflects a real condition or noisy/templated logging, and tune log levels so genuine reconciliation failures are not masked.</summary>
</requirement>
</requirements>
<riskLevel>high</riskLevel>
</invoke>
